lessons.title: Short Notes
lessons.notes_html:
What is Yaum-e-Takbeer?

Yaum-e-Takbeer is observed on 28 May every year to mark the day in 1998 when Pakistan carried out its nuclear tests at Chaghi, Balochistan, in response to India's tests. The tests made Pakistan the seventh nuclear power in the world and the first Muslim country with nuclear capability. The day is celebrated as a symbol of national defence and self-reliance.

Three Basic Objectives of the Local Government System of General Pervez Musharraf

Three basic objectives of General Pervez Musharraf's Local Government system (2001) were: to bring government closer to the people by devolving power to the district and union levels; to ensure people's participation in development decisions through elected local councils; and to improve delivery of basic services such as health, education, water and sanitation at the grassroots level.

Five Main Projects of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf Government

Five main projects of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf government (2018 onwards) were: the Ehsaas Programme for poverty relief and social protection; the Naya Pakistan Housing Programme for low-cost houses; the Sehat Sahulat (Health Card) Programme for free medical treatment; the Ten Billion Tree Tsunami for tree plantation and environment; and the Kamyab Jawan Programme of loans and skills training for youth.

Significance of the Motorway

The Motorway (M-2, Lahore-Islamabad, opened in 1997) is significant because it reduced travel time between major cities, improved road safety, and promoted trade, tourism and economic activity along its route. It became a model for modern road infrastructure in Pakistan, and later motorways linked other cities, strengthening national connectivity.

How is the President of Pakistan Elected?

The President of Pakistan is elected by an electoral college consisting of the members of the Senate, the National Assembly, and the four Provincial Assemblies. The election is held by secret ballot, and the candidate who secures the majority of votes of the electoral college is declared elected as President for a term of five years.

lessons.title: Detailed Notes
lessons.notes_html:
Agricultural and Industrial Reforms of Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto

Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto's agricultural reforms included land reforms that fixed a ceiling on land holdings and distributed surplus land among landless farmers, and support for small farmers through credit and inputs. His industrial reforms included nationalization of major industries, banks, insurance companies and educational institutions, to bring the economy under state control for the benefit of the common man. He also set up the State Life Insurance Corporation and promoted labour welfare, raising wages and introducing group insurance and social security for workers.

Industrial, Economic and Social Reforms of Pervez Musharraf

Pervez Musharraf's industrial and economic reforms included privatization of state enterprises, liberalization of trade and banking, promotion of information technology and telecommunications, and policies that raised foreign investment and GDP growth. His social reforms included the Local Government system of 2001, devolution of power to districts, women's representation in councils and assemblies, and steps for education and health, along with media liberalization that expanded private television channels.

Benazir Bhutto's Two Terms: Which Era Was Better for People?

Benazir Bhutto's second term (1993-96) is generally considered better for the people than her first term (1988-90), because her government lasted longer and could carry out more programmes. In the second term, the People's Works Programme, Lady Health Workers scheme, polio eradication campaign, Eighth Development Plan and new energy policy were launched, and Pakistan rejoined the Commonwealth. Her first term was cut short after less than two years, limiting what could be achieved.

Economic Reforms of Mian Nawaz Sharif

Mian Nawaz Sharif's economic reforms included an industrial policy (1990) encouraging the private sector, a privatization commission (1991) to sell loss-making state units, an agricultural policy giving relief to farmers (including waiving import duty on machinery), and major infrastructure projects such as the Lahore-Islamabad Motorway. His government also launched the Ghazi-Barotha and other energy projects, promoted foreign investment, and in 1998 responded to sanctions after the nuclear tests with economic measures to stabilize the country.

Salient Features of the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan

Salient features of the 1973 Constitution are: it declares Pakistan an Islamic Republic with Islam as the state religion; it provides a parliamentary form of government with the Prime Minister as head of government and the President as head of state; it guarantees fundamental rights to citizens; it gives provincial autonomy with a federal structure; it provides an independent judiciary; it makes Urdu the national language; and it includes the Objectives Resolution as its preamble, protecting Islamic provisions and the rights of minorities.

lessons.title: Short Notes
lessons.notes_html:
What is Meant by Foreign Policy?

Foreign policy is the set of principles and decisions by which a country conducts its relations with other countries and international organizations. It aims to protect national interests, security and sovereignty, promote trade and economic cooperation, and maintain friendly relations, while following the country's ideology and values.

Names of the Central Asian Republics

The Central Asian Republics are: Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan. All five became independent after the breakup of the Soviet Union in 1991, and Pakistan has developed trade, energy and cultural relations with them.

Importance of Gwadar Port

Gwadar port is important because it lies at the mouth of the Persian Gulf, giving Pakistan a deep-sea port near the world's main oil shipping route. It provides China and Central Asian states a short trade route to the Arabian Sea through CPEC. It is expected to become a regional trade hub, creating jobs and boosting Pakistan's economy.

What is the Palestine Problem?

The Palestine problem is the dispute over the land of Palestine between Arabs (Palestinians) and Israel, which began when Israel was created in 1948 and large numbers of Palestinians were displaced from their homes. Pakistan supports the right of Palestinians to an independent state with Al-Quds (Jerusalem) as its capital, and the issue remains a central concern of the Muslim world and the OIC.

Why are the Land and Sea Routes of Pakistan Important?

Pakistan's land and sea routes are important because Pakistan lies at the crossroads of South Asia, Central Asia, China and the Gulf, so all trade between these regions can pass through it. Its seaports at Karachi and Gwadar connect Europe and Asia by sea, while its land routes (including the Karakoram Highway to China) give landlocked Afghanistan and Central Asia access to the sea, making Pakistan's location strategically and economically vital.

lessons.title: Detailed Notes
lessons.notes_html:
Main Objectives of Pakistan's Foreign Policy

The main objectives of Pakistan's foreign policy are: protection of the ideology of Pakistan and its sovereignty and territorial integrity; promotion of peace and friendly relations with all countries, especially neighbours; support for the Kashmir cause and the right of self-determination of Kashmiris; solidarity with Muslim countries and the Muslim Ummah; promotion of economic cooperation, trade and development; and contribution to world peace through the United Nations and peacekeeping.

Importance of the Kashmir Issue in Pak-India Relations

The Kashmir issue is the central dispute in Pak-India relations and the main cause of tension and wars between the two countries since 1947. Pakistan holds that Kashmiris should decide their future by a plebiscite promised by UN resolutions, while India controls part of Kashmir by force. Because both countries are nuclear powers, an unresolved Kashmir dispute threatens regional and world peace, and no lasting friendship is possible without its just solution.

Pakistan's Relations with Turkey

Pakistan and Turkey enjoy deep brotherly relations based on common religion, history and culture, going back to the support of Turkish Muslims for the Khilafat Movement and of Pakistanis for Turkey's freedom struggle. Both countries cooperate in defence, trade, education and culture, support each other on Kashmir and Cyprus issues, and are members of the OIC and ECO. Turkey has supported Pakistan in difficult times, including after earthquakes and floods.

Role of China in the Construction and Development of Pakistan

China has played a major role in Pakistan's development: it built the Karakoram Highway linking the two countries, helped build the Gwadar port, and is investing billions in CPEC projects including roads, railways, power plants and special economic zones. China has also helped in defence production (such as the JF-17 aircraft), nuclear power plants, and trade, and has consistently supported Pakistan on Kashmir and in international forums.

Pakistan-US Relations

Pakistan-US relations have passed through phases of close cooperation and strain. The US gave Pakistan military and economic aid during the Cold War and the Afghan wars of the 1980s and after 2001, while Pakistan helped in the fight against terrorism. Relations have also faced tensions over issues such as the nuclear programme, Afghanistan, and aid conditions. Despite ups and downs, both countries continue to cooperate in trade, education, counter-terrorism and regional stability.

lessons.title: Key Facts
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Head Islam has been constructed on the River Sutlej.
  • The 2nd Five Year Plan was started in 1960 to speed up economic growth.
  • Vast salt deposits are found in Kohistan Namak (the Salt Range).
  • Sprinkler and drip irrigation is the efficient and modern method of watering.
  • Tarbela Dam, on the Indus, is the largest earth-filled dam; Mangla Dam is on the Jhelum.
  • From 2008 to 2018 GDP growth first fell to about 2-3 percent, then improved to about 5-6 percent.

lessons.title: Short Notes
lessons.notes_html:
Define Economic Development

Economic development is the sustained ability of an economy to generate higher national income and improve the living standard of its people. It is measured not only by growth in GDP but also by better employment, education, health, and per capita income, so that poverty decreases and people enjoy a better quality of life.

Main Reason for the Decrease of Foreign Investment in Pakistan

The main reason for the decrease of foreign investment in Pakistan has been the uncertain security situation and political instability, including terrorism after 2001, which made investors afraid of losses. Other reasons are energy shortages, weak infrastructure, complicated rules, and the economic sanctions Pakistan faced after the 1998 nuclear tests.

What is Meant by Manpower? Who are Included in Manpower?

Manpower means the total labour force of a country that is able and willing to work. It includes all employed and unemployed persons of working age (usually 15 to 64 years) in agriculture, industry, services, government and self-employment, both skilled and unskilled, men and women.

What is Meant by Defence Industry?

Defence industry means the industries that produce weapons, equipment and supplies for the armed forces, such as aircraft, tanks, ships, ammunition and uniforms. In Pakistan, defence production includes Pakistan Ordnance Factories (Wah), Heavy Industries Taxila, and Pakistan Aeronautical Complex (Kamra), which reduce dependence on imports and also create jobs and technology.

Names of Five Link Canals

Five link canals of Pakistan are: the Rasul-Qadirabad Link Canal, the Qadirabad-Balloki Link Canal, the Balloki-Sulemanki Link Canal, the Trimmu-Sidhnai Link Canal, and the Chashma-Jhelum Link Canal. These canals transfer water from western rivers to eastern rivers under the Indus Waters Treaty arrangements.

lessons.title: Detailed Notes
lessons.notes_html:
Economic Growth from 2008 to 2018

From 2008 to 2018, Pakistan's economy faced slow growth at first due to the global financial crisis, energy shortages, terrorism and political instability, with GDP growth falling to around 2-3 percent. Later, growth improved to about 5-6 percent as security improved, CPEC projects began, and remittances from overseas Pakistanis increased. However, the trade deficit widened, foreign debt grew, and inflation and unemployment remained problems, so growth did not fully reach the poor.

Dams, Barrages and Canals on the Indus River

On the Indus River system, the main dams are Tarbela Dam (on the Indus, the largest earth-filled dam), Mangla Dam (on the Jhelum), and Diamer-Basha (under construction). Important barrages are Sukkur, Guddu, Kotri, Taunsa, Chashma and Jinnah barrages, which divert river water into canals. The canal system includes perennial and non-perennial canals and link canals that carry water to the fields of Punjab and Sindh, making Pakistan's irrigation system one of the largest in the world.

Important Minerals of Pakistan

Important minerals of Pakistan are: coal (found in Thar, Lakhra and Duki, used for power), natural gas (Sui, the main energy source), oil (Potwar and Sindh), iron ore (Kalabagh), copper and gold (Saindak and Reko Diq in Balochistan), chromite (Muslim Bagh), salt (Khewra in the Salt Range), gypsum, limestone (for cement), and marble (Khyber Pakhtunkhwa). These minerals support industry, energy and exports, but many remain under-explored.

Problems Faced by Agriculture and Suggestions to Solve Them

Problems of agriculture are: shortage and wastage of irrigation water, small and divided land holdings, outdated farming methods, expensive inputs (seed, fertilizer), lack of credit for small farmers, waterlogging and salinity, and poor marketing and storage. Suggestions are: line water channels to save water, use modern methods (sprinkler and drip irrigation, laser levelling), provide easy loans and quality seeds, consolidate holdings, control waterlogging by drainage, and improve roads, storage and markets for farmers.

Positive Effects of Increase in Crop Yields on the Economy

Higher crop yields increase farmers' incomes and food supply, reduce food imports and prices, and provide more raw material for agro-industries such as sugar, textile and food processing. They increase exports of cotton, rice and fruits, earn foreign exchange, create rural jobs, reduce poverty, and raise GDP and the overall living standard.

Main Reasons of Trade Deficit and How to Get Rid of the Problem

Trade deficit arises because Pakistan imports more (oil, machinery, chemicals) than it exports (mainly textiles, rice, leather). Reasons are: narrow export base, low value-added products, high oil import bill, and low competitiveness. To reduce it, Pakistan should diversify exports, add value to textiles and agriculture, develop import substitutes, promote IT and remittances, control unnecessary imports, and improve energy and industrial productivity.

How Poverty Can Be Decreased by Promoting Small Industries

Small industries decrease poverty because they need little capital and create many jobs, especially in rural and small-town areas where large factories do not exist. They use local raw materials and skills (such as sports goods in Sialkot, cutlery in Wazirabad, and pottery in Multan), raise incomes of poor families, reduce migration to cities, and increase exports. Government support through loans, training and markets makes them even more effective against poverty.

Ways to Increase Energy Resources in the Country

Ways to increase energy resources are: build more dams for hydel power (Diamer-Basha, Dasu), develop Thar coal for power generation, expand solar and wind power (especially in Sindh and Balochistan), explore new oil and gas fields, save energy by efficient appliances and reducing line losses, and import energy through projects such as CASA-1000 and the Iran-Pakistan gas pipeline, while promoting conservation.

Why Ports and Dry Ports are Necessary for International Trade

Ports and dry ports are necessary because almost all of Pakistan's foreign trade moves by sea, and ports (Karachi, Port Qasim, Gwadar) load and unload ships, store goods and connect to world shipping. Dry ports (Lahore, Sialkot, Faisalabad, Multan, Peshawar, Quetta) bring port facilities inland, so exporters can clear customs near their factories, reducing transport cost, congestion at seaports, and time, which increases trade and employment.

lessons.title: Short Notes
lessons.notes_html:
Five Problems of Education in Pakistan

Five problems of education in Pakistan are: low literacy rate and high dropout, especially of girls; shortage of trained teachers and schools in rural areas; outdated curriculum and rote learning; lack of funds and poor buildings, furniture and facilities; and the gap between public and private education, with different standards and languages of instruction.

What is Gender Discrimination?

Gender discrimination is unfair treatment of a person because of their gender, for example giving boys preference over girls in education, jobs, health care and inheritance. It limits women's opportunities and participation in society, and it is against the Constitution, which guarantees equality of all citizens.

What is Meant by Co-curricular Activities?

Co-curricular activities are activities carried out along with studies, outside the classroom, such as sports, debates, quizzes, scouting, drama, art and school trips. They develop students' physical health, confidence, leadership, teamwork and talents, and make education complete beyond textbooks.

Names of Three Punjabi Poets

Three famous Punjabi poets are: Baba Bulleh Shah, known for his Sufi poetry (Kafian); Waris Shah, author of the epic Heer Ranjha; and Mian Muhammad Bakhsh, author of Saif-ul-Malook. Other well-known Punjabi poets are Sultan Bahu and Khawaja Ghulam Farid.

How Can Balance be Created Between Population and Resources?

Balance between population and resources can be created by slowing population growth through education (especially of girls), family planning and health services, while increasing resources through better agriculture, industry, energy and jobs. If population grows slower than food, water, jobs and services, the pressure on resources falls and living standards improve.

lessons.title: Detailed Notes
lessons.notes_html:
Suggestions to Solve Problems of Education in Pakistan

Suggestions to solve education problems are: increase the education budget and build more schools, especially for girls in rural areas; train and fairly pay teachers; update the curriculum to modern needs with science and technology; provide free textbooks, meals and transport to reduce dropouts; enforce compulsory primary education; and reduce the gap between public and private schools by a uniform standard.

How Similarities in Regional Cultures Promote National Harmony

Pakistan's regional cultures (Punjabi, Sindhi, Balochi, Pashtun, Kashmiri and others) share many similarities: common Islamic values, similar family systems, respect for elders, hospitality, love of poetry and music, and shared festivals such as Eid. These similarities help people of different provinces understand and respect each other, reduce prejudice, and strengthen the feeling of being one nation despite different languages and customs.

Important Attributes of Pakistani Society

Important attributes of Pakistani society are: Islam as the common faith and basis of values; strong family system with respect for elders; hospitality and generosity towards guests; love for the homeland and national unity; rich cultural diversity in languages, dress, food and arts; and a tradition of helping others in difficulty, as seen in charity and community work.

National and Two Regional Languages in Detail

The national language of Pakistan is Urdu, which is understood across the country, is the medium of national communication, media and literature, and unites people of all provinces. Two regional languages are: Punjabi, spoken by the largest number of people in Punjab, rich in Sufi poetry (Bulleh Shah, Waris Shah); and Sindhi, spoken in Sindh, with a long literary tradition (Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai, Sachal Sarmast) and its own script. Both regional languages are taught in schools and used in provincial assemblies and media.

Significance of Tourism in Pakistan

Tourism is significant because Pakistan has mountains (K-2, Nanga Parbat), valleys (Hunza, Swat), historical sites (Mohenjo-daro, Taxila, Lahore Fort) and religious places that attract visitors. In 2019 about 50 million Pakistanis toured within the country. Tourism earns foreign exchange, creates jobs in hotels, transport and handicrafts, promotes the country's soft image, and helps people of different regions understand each other.

Gender Distribution of Population in Pakistan

In Pakistan's population, males slightly outnumber females (about 51 percent male and 49 percent female in recent censuses), giving a sex ratio of about 105 males per 100 females. This imbalance is due to higher female mortality in the past, preference for sons, and under-reporting of women. In urban areas the gap is larger because men migrate to cities for work, while rural areas are more balanced.

Problems of the Health Sector and Ways to Solve Them

Problems of the health sector are: shortage of hospitals, doctors and medicines in rural areas; high cost of treatment for the poor; unclean water and poor sanitation causing disease; lack of awareness about hygiene and vaccination; and overcrowded public hospitals. Solutions are: increase health budget, build rural health centres and train Lady Health Workers, provide clean water and sanitation, run vaccination and awareness campaigns, and expand health insurance like the Sehat Card.

Role of Minorities in Economic Development of Pakistan

Minorities have played an important role in Pakistan's economic development: Christian, Hindu, Parsi and Sikh communities have served in trade, industry, education, health and civil service. Examples from the chapter are: Justice A. R. Cornelius in law and the Constitution, Dr. Ruth Pfau in health (leprosy control), and minority officers in the armed forces. Their skills, businesses and services contribute to the economy, and their participation strengthens national unity.

Main Features of Pakistani Culture

Main features of Pakistani culture are: Islamic values and way of life as its foundation; diversity of languages (Urdu, Punjabi, Sindhi, Pashto, Balochi, etc.); traditional dress (shalwar kameez, with regional variations); rich literature, poetry, music (qawwali, folk songs) and arts (truck art, pottery, embroidery); love of sports, especially cricket and hockey; hospitality, respect for elders, and joint family system; and festivals such as Eid-ul-Fitr, Eid-ul-Azha, and national days (23 March, 14 August).
